body.statement: For every fixed \(C_v<\infty\), compactness and linearity give \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty<\infty\). Because \(\delta_q>0\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty/\sqrt n<\delta_q\), so every positive or negative coordinate tilt obeys \(q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v)\ge q^0_{ax\ell}-|s(h,v)_{ax\ell}|/\sqrt n>\eta\). Uniformly on that domain, \(q_n(h,v)\in(\Delta_{L-1})^{2K}\), \(P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p)\), and \(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\). Moreover, for every bounded \(u\), some bounded nuisance coordinate \(v\) satisfies \(\sqrt n\{\tau(q_n(h,v))-\tau(q^0)\}=Qh+Nu\), while the remaining coordinates range over every common-arm-mean and zero-mean outcome-shape direction.
body.justification: This theorem verifies that the entire \(Qh+Nu\) treatment-effect fiber and every remaining shape nuisance form a legal local submodel rather than an assumed least-favorable family.
body.gap: Hirano and Porter localize regular models but do not construct the saturated finite-support fiber under design-dependent annotation.
body.consumer: The nuisance-uniform lower bound uses the full fiber, including every treatment-effect and outcome-shape tangent that leaves policy contrasts unchanged.
